Container.Name: nazgarr
Container.Overview:
Nazgarr manages your media library, torrent seeding folders, the hardlink correspondence between them, the real state of your configured torrent clients (multi-client, cross-seed included), and publishing new uploads to trackers - all in one place.
Web UI on http://[IP]:[PORT:8080]: dashboard, library (poster and folder views), torrent files, reseeding review queue, uploads to your trackers (identification, dupe check, release names per tracker, queue and history) and configuration. This template uses the :stable image; switch the Repository to :nightly to follow every test build.
Follows the TrashGuide layout: mount your combined torrents+media folder at /data, same as your download client and media manager - this is what makes hardlinks between them work. Only two paths are needed: Config (appdata) and Data (your library). No need to edit any file: every folder you mount is proposed as a disk in Settings › Storage. Separate disks instead of the share? Remove Data and add one Path per disk (/mnt/disk1 → /mnt/disk1, …), never next to the share.
On first start, if config/config.yaml doesn't exist yet in the "Config" folder below, the container creates it from config.example.yaml with default values.

Config.Name: Config
Config.Description: Appdata: config.yaml (created from config.example.yaml on first start if missing) and the app's own SQLite database/cache

Config.Name: Data
Config.Description: TrashGuide-style combined torrents+media folder - mount the SAME host path you use for your download client and media manager, so hardlinks between them work. Added as a disk from Configuration › Storage after the first start.

Config.Name: PUID
Config.Description: User ID the web process runs as (99 = nobody on Unraid, matching Sonarr/Radarr/qBittorrent)

Config.Name: PGID
Config.Description: Group ID the web process runs as (100 = users on Unraid)

Config.Name: APP_SECRET_KEY
Config.Description: Key used to encrypt credentials stored in the database at rest (tracker tokens, torrent client passwords). Generate with: openssl rand -base64 32 | tr '+/' '-_' (works out of the box on macOS and Unraid, no extra dependency needed).
